memory_candidates: GeneralExistPartOrdered atomMap 0 is FALSE (not just unprovable). Counterexample: Z (integers) with 1 constant predicate, r=2, env_nfs = constant (all Z-points have same depth-1 1-var NF), env_atoms = 'e(0)<e(1)', ssn = between-zone. env=[0,2] gives existential TRUE (y=1), env=[0,1] gives existential FALSE (no integer between 0 and 1). temporal_truth Z atomMap 0 A is fixed for any formula A, so the biconditional fails.

Root cause: a closed temporal formula evaluated at e(0) cannot characterize an existential that depends on the gap structure between env elements. On Z-homogeneous structures, all temporal formulas at any point have the same truth value, but between-zone existentials depend on the quantitative gap.

GeneralExistPartIndiv (without orders) is ALSO false, but for a different reason: temporal formula at e(0) can't detect order of other env elements. Both variants fail because the single evaluation point lacks information about the env configuration.

The k=0 case of KampBypass works WITHOUT GeneralExistPartOrdered (uses enriched_bypass_until/since infrastructure, ~2300 lines). Only the k>=1 case (existPart_succ_n1_bypass, succ k' branch) uses GeneralExistPartOrdered. This is the code that needs restructuring.

existPart_succ_n1_bypass is sorry-free assuming ih_general_exist. Since ih_general_exist = GeneralExistPartOrdered (which is false), the theorem is vacuously true from a false hypothesis. The KampBypass proof for k>=1 is currently unsound.
